Held-out stopping iterations, ACT/HOLD decisions, pose-error task outcomes, and machine-specific timing readouts.

Q2_record_separates: Within the declared numerical generator, task-conditioned stopping can be compared with fixed, full, and estimator-side stopping on the same held-out trajectories.
The record separates in-distribution behavior from a declared 2x sensor-noise stress condition.
The finite completion-envelope record separates latent pose identity from task-reader invariance: multiple retained pose completions can yield the same task verdict.
The trajectory-calibration record separates an observable proxy from an empirically calibrated completion bound: the proxy itself is not treated as a posterior or confidence interval.

The trajectory-level held-out coverage readout can test whether the frozen envelope contains all six hidden pose-error coordinates at all retained stages of an episode within the declared numerical generator.
The record does not separate numerical-backend behavior from real RGB-D/GPU/robot behavior, and calibrated marginal episode coverage does not establish deterministic safety.
Q3_ai_filled: The AI assistant drafted and revised the public experiment code, test harness, statistical summaries, documentation, and manuscript wording under the founder-selected research problem and hypothesis.

Task thresholds, split protocol, calibration design, stress-test implementation, numerical floors, and episode-level nonconformity construction were proposed during AI-assisted development and are disclosed as design choices, not source facts.

The admissible-completion-set, task-reader-image, robust-verdict, reader-diameter, refinement-contraction, finite-completion, trajectory-nonconformity, calibration-scale, calibrated-box, and coverage-qualified-stop equations C1-C10 are NEW project definitions/derivations proposed during AI-assisted development; they are not existing Toledo equations.
Split conformal prediction is an external statistical method used as a calibration basis; it is neither invented by this project nor attributed to Toledo.
Q4_assumed: Generated asymmetric point clouds are an adequate numerical fixture for testing iterative rigid-registration stopping logic.
Nearest-neighbour point-to-point ICP with damped Kabsch updates is a useful iterative pose-refinement proxy.
The local linearized dispersion quantity is only an observable proxy; it is not silently promoted to a calibrated posterior or confidence interval.
Calibration and held-out episodes are exchangeable only within the declared in-distribution synthetic generator; the 2x noise stress condition intentionally violates that match.
The fixed per-coordinate numerical floors in the trajectory nonconformity score are regularizers selected for this fixture, not physical constants.
Episode-level split-conformal calibration licenses a marginal coverage interpretation only under its statistical assumptions; it is not a deterministic safety certificate.
The finite completion set is a retained computational construction of still-admissible alternatives, not a claim that every member exists or that the set has complete latent coverage.
Center-plus-vertices is sufficient only for the current monotone absolute-value toy task readers; no such exactness is claimed for arbitrary manipulation tasks.
Wall-clock timing is machine-specific and secondary to iteration counts and independent ground-truth task outcomes.
